lines: A good shield is a promise you test before anyone needs it.
I once fixed a helmet so dented it looked like it had argued with the ground.
After a raid, you learn which buckles were honest and which only looked brave.
There is a story from the forge, but it sounds smaller unless you were standing there.
Most stories here begin with someone saying, 'It will only take a moment.' They are always wrong.
I remember the smell of rain, the sound of the bell, and everyone suddenly pretending they had a plan.
The funny part came later. At the time, nobody was laughing.
A village story changes depending on who got embarrassed in it.
I could make it grand, but honestly, it was mostly mud, noise, and bad timing.
Still, we tell it because we made it through, and that makes people stand a little straighter.
Once a shield came back with three arrows in it and one very grateful owner behind it.
I saw a helmet save a life because someone had listened about the strap.
A young guard once asked for armor that made them look taller. The knees gave them away.
One winter the forge froze at the door and still somehow stayed too hot inside.
There was a <red><bold>raid</bold></red> where every repaired shield came home scratched and proud.
I once hammered a dent flat and found half a story hiding under it.
A traveler brought me a breastplate so rusty it seemed offended by daylight.
The bell rang while I was quenching a plate. The steam looked braver than I felt.
I made greaves for someone who claimed they never run. They wore out the knees first.
One golem stood by the forge all night after a bad attack. Nobody asked it to leave.
A shield cracked during practice and saved someone from trusting it later.
I once traded armor for bread during a hard week. Both of us thought we won.
There was a helmet with a chicken feather caught in it for days. Nobody confessed.
A child tried to lift a chestplate and declared war on gravity.
The old forge door still squeals like it remembers every emergency.
